hero.title: Jain Architecture: A Deep Dive
hero.description: An analytical study of the evolutionary phases of Jain cave temples, structural shrines, and the architectural evolution from the Mauryan to the Medieval period.

timeline.title: The Chronological Framework
timeline.description: Evolution of Jain architecture from rock-cut caves to majestic marble temples.

cards.details: Earliest examples of Jain rock-cut architecture in the Barabar and Nagarjuni hills, initially patronized by Mauryan rulers.
Development of Udayagiri and Khandagiri caves in Odisha, reflecting structural sophistication under the Chedi dynasty.
Golden era of Jain temple building, characterized by intricate marble carvings at Dilwara and Ranakpur.

items.title: K.O.D
items.decryption: Remembers the key patron (Kharavela), the site (Odisha caves), and the pinnacle of architecture (Dilwara).

traps.title: UPSC Common Exam Traps
items: Assuming all caves in India are Buddhist; remember Udayagiri/Khandagiri are Jain.
Confusing Maru-Gurjara style solely with Hinduism; it is heavily associated with Jain temple architecture in Rajasthan/Gujarat.

sections.title: 1. Core Study Notes
sections.content:
Geography

  • Udayagiri-Khandagiri (Odisha)
  • Dilwara (Mount Abu)
  • Ranakpur (Rajasthan)
  • Ellora/Aihole (Deccan)

Personalities

  • Kharavela (Chedi Dynasty)
  • Vimal Shah (Dilwara Patron)
  • Solanki Rulers

Architectural Evolution Mindmap

  • Cave Architecture
    • Earliest phase
    • Natural caverns modified for monks
    • Udayagiri/Khandagiri caves
  • Structural Temples
    • Temple City model (e.g., Palitana)
    • Use of white marble
    • Intricate 'Jali' work
FeatureJain TempleBuddhist Chaitya
Primary deityTirthankaraStupa/Buddha
Common elementMandapaVihara
